houses.name: Dior

houses.name: Tom Ford

houses.name: Chanel

houses.name: Yves Saint Laurent

houses.name: Ajmal Perfumes India
houses.description: Luxury Oud, Attar & EDP Fragrances — Ajmal's India storefront ('75 Years Legacy', 'Farm to Fragrance'); brand ambassadors Ranveer Singh, Saif Ali Khan. Legal entity AJMAL & SONS, Mumbai.

houses.name: House of EM5
houses.description: Clone house (EM5 Formulations Pvt. Ltd., 2/1 Peki Mundla, Nemawar Road, Palda, Indore MP 452020) selling inspired EDPs around Rs.449-499 for 50ml plus an original extrait-strength 'Private Blends' line. Products labeled Vegan | Cruelty Free | Clean. Self-described 'best perfume brand in India'.

houses.name: My Perfume Secrets
houses.description: 'World's Most Affordable Luxury Fragrance Brand'. Sells extrait de parfum at 25%+ oil concentration starting at 8ml. Every product page states an 'Inspired By' original and an 'Accuracy: X% close to the original' claim (brand claims, not independent findings). Address: Kalbadevi, Mumbai 400002. 159 products in /collections/all.

houses.name: Dupify
houses.description: Budget clone label (dupify.in). 53 perfumes, each with 3 variants (Attar 12ml, Perfume 20ml/55ml). 3 explicit inspired-by mappings. Researched 2026-10-02.

houses.name: RZLER
houses.description: Indian dupe house (perfume.rzler.com). 43 products (41 perfumes + 2 discovery sets) with explicit inspired-by mappings (39). All marked sold out on 2026-10-02. Researched 2026-10-02.

houses.name: Arabian Aroma
houses.description: Kanpur clone house (arabianaroma.co.in). 238 products. Prices are collection 'From' prices; exact size unconfirmed. Only 1 explicit inspired-by mapping. Researched 2026-10-02.

houses.name: Eau de Zidaan
houses.description: Mumbai artisan house founded by perfumer Zaid; reportedly 20,000+ bottles sold since launch. Details to be verified.

houses.name: XLNC Perfumery
houses.description: 'Buy Best Premium Perfume for Men & Women Online India' — a clone house selling 'Inspired Perfume' SKUs coded XPnn; each product card carries a write-up about the original designer fragrance. One product notes 'Concentration: 35%'. ~141 products in the Inspired Perfume collection.

houses.name: Celestial Perfume
houses.description: Surat clone house (celestialperfume.in). 104 products (73 perfumes, 20 attars, 9 gourmet, 2 gift sets). 70 explicit inspired-by mappings. 27 duplicate -copy listings excluded. Researched 2026-10-02.

houses.name: Purenso Select
houses.description: Designer-inspired fragrance OILS (not sprays) at ₹225–₹275. Oil format — performance notes in our tests reflect oil wear, not spray.

houses.name: Naso Profumi
houses.description: Contemporary niche perfumes with natural ingredients — 'a journey where tradition meets luxury, and every scent tells a story'; traditional deg & bhapka distillation, IFRA compliant, made in India. Address: C/o M/s Peco Perfumers, B-1/50, Sector-G, Aliganj, Lucknow 226024.

houses.name: The Inkpot Perfumes
houses.description: Indian indie perfumery. Details to be verified.

houses.name: Sugandhco
houses.description: Heritage brand 'with a legacy & experience of 170+ years' — 'a family business since 1850'. Online store SCENTKART selling high-quality, vegan & safe perfumes, attars and home fragrances.

houses.name: Gulab Singh Johrimal
houses.description: Over two centuries of aromatic excellence: established 1816 by Lala Gulab Singh and Lala Johrimal, a traditional perfumery in Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi once serving royal Nawaabs and nobility, now run by the eighth generation. Address: 320, Dariba Kalan, Delhi 110006.

houses.name: Boond Fragrances
houses.description: An Indian brand co-founded in 2021 with the mission to revive the ancient art of Indian perfume making. Handcrafted, alcohol-free natural attars made in Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh using the centuries-old Deg-Bhapka method; conferred the Geographical Indicator (GI) Tag by the Government of India for authentic Kannauj Perfume. Address: Khasra no. 208, Vill and PO Behrin, Tirwa Road, Kannauj (UP)-209727.

houses.name: Asam & Co Perfumers
houses.description: 114-year-old Kannauj perfumers, specialists in Shamama attar.

houses.name: Lala Kedarnath Khattri & Sons
houses.description: 115-year-old Kannauj house — among the oldest attar makers in India.

houses.name: ARUN Mradul Perfumers

houses.name: Gauri Sugandh
houses.description: 45-year-old Kannauj house producing attars and natural perfumery oils.

houses.name: Pooja Perfumery & Exports
houses.description: 54-year-old Kannauj manufacturer and exporter of attars and fragrances.

houses.name: Bombay Perfumery
houses.description: A contemporary fragrance house based out of Mumbai offering progressive perfumery. Its EDPs are Indian at heart, modern in aesthetic and unique in experience; crafted by renowned international perfumers. Claims a 30-year legacy in the fragrance business. Address: 31 Manoj Industrial Estate, G D Ambekar Road, Wadala, Mumbai 400031.

houses.name: SKINN by Titan
houses.description: Titan's fragrance brand. Runs #NotesFromAPerfumer featuring principal perfumer Ilias Ermenidis, 'the creative genius behind SKINN Noura perfumes'. Collections: Raw, Verge, Sheer, Celeste, Nude, Steele, Pristine, Tales, Noura, Nox, Amalfi, Escapade, 247.

houses.name: NEESH
houses.description: A haute perfumery house selling luxury Extrait De Parfum for men and women online, with 7-day easy returns. Fragrances created with perfumer Julien Rasquinet. The site's 'Our Story' traces its roots to 1904.

houses.name: Forest Essentials
houses.description: Luxury Ayurvedic beauty brand — 'a pioneer in the beauty industry, the first brand to combine traditional Ayurvedic practices with modern aesthetics'; products handcrafted using natural ingredients sourced from India; PETA approved, Ayush/GMP/ISO certified.

houses.name: Scentedelic
houses.description: 'SOURCED WITH INTEGRITY, CRAFTED FOR EXCELLENCE' — small-batch perfumery where 'each ingredient is carefully macerated'; fragrances 'charged with positive energy and blessings'; cruelty-free; all scents unisex. Sells Parfum Extrait in 50ml bottles. Contact: +91-6355869747.

houses.name: Heavenduft
houses.description: 'Artisan Perfume House' founded 23 June 2020 by independent perfumer Tausif Iqbal Shaikh. Artisan perfumes crafted with natural oils, pure attars, agarwood and sandalwood oils — original creations, not clones. Address: Sewree, Wadala, Mumbai 400031.

houses.name: Perfume Oil Corner
houses.description: Sells 30ml bottles of 'inspired by' perfumes at a standard Rs.650. Claim on product pages: '98.5% exact same aroma' and '80% concentrated perfume oils' (brand claims, not independent findings). Also sells sample sets and 'inspired by' attars.

houses.name: Bella Vita Luxury
houses.description: Mass-market perfume brand (bellavitaorganic.com) — large affordable fragrance catalog: EDPs, minis, gift sets, pocket sprays. No inspired-by claims on the site; original affordable creations.

perfumes.name: Aventus
perfumes.description: The king of niche. Smoky pineapple and birch over a musky base — the most complimented and most cloned masculine scent in India.

perfumes.name: Sauvage Eau de Toilette
perfumes.description: The modern fresh-spicy icon. Bergamot and pepper over ambroxan — loud, radiant, and everywhere, which is exactly why India hunts its dupes.

perfumes.name: Sauvage Elixir
perfumes.description: Sauvage turned up to eleven — a dense spicy elixir with a famous licorice twist. Beast-mode performance, premium price.

perfumes.name: Stronger With You Intensely
perfumes.description: Molten vanilla-spice hug. Sweet, warm and effortlessly attractive — a date-night staple across Indian metros.

perfumes.name: Acqua di Gio
perfumes.description: The original aquatic. Mediterranean citrus and sea notes — the safe fresh scent a generation of Indian men grew up on.

perfumes.name: Tobacco Vanille
perfumes.description: The cozy icon. Honeyed pipe tobacco drowned in vanilla and dried fruits — winter in a bottle, and a dupe-house rite of passage.

perfumes.name: Oud Wood
perfumes.description: Oud for people who fear oud — smooth sandalwood and cardamom around a polite agarwood core. Understated luxury.

perfumes.name: Interlude Man
perfumes.description: Controlled chaos — smoky incense, oregano and leather in a blue-bottle storm. The connoisseur’s powerhouse.

perfumes.name: Reflection Man
perfumes.description: Sunshine in a flacon — sparkling florals over creamy woods. Effortless elegance, terrible value debates aside.

perfumes.name: Bleu de Chanel Parfum
perfumes.description: The classy gentleman, perfected. Citrus-woods of extraordinary polish — the office-luxury benchmark India clones relentlessly.

perfumes.name: Allure Homme Sport Eau Extreme
perfumes.description: Sporty freshness with a sweet tonka backbone — the gym-to-office crossover India loves.

perfumes.name: Y Eau de Parfum
perfumes.description: Blue-juice freshness with a sweet aromatic core — the modern crowd-pleaser.

perfumes.name: 1 Million
perfumes.description: The gold-bar party bomb. Cinnamon, leather and amber turned to maximum — India’s wedding-season weapon.

perfumes.name: Invictus
perfumes.description: The aquatic trophy. Marine freshness with a woody-amber drydown — sporty, loud, youthful.

perfumes.name: Eros
perfumes.description: Mint-apple freshness melting into vanilla-tonka sweetness. The club scent of a generation.

perfumes.name: Dylan Blue
perfumes.description: Mediterranean aromatic freshness with a peppery bite — versatile and modern.

perfumes.name: Bad Boy
perfumes.description: Sweet-spicy duality in a lightning-bolt bottle. Cocoa-tonka warmth with peppery crackle.

perfumes.name: Le Male Le Parfum
perfumes.description: The sailor, dressed for winter. Powdery iris-lavender over deep vanilla — the definitive cold-weather designer.

perfumes.name: Baccarat Rouge 540
perfumes.description: The crystal-amber phenomenon. Saffron and amberwood in radiant, airy sweetness — the most cloned fragrance on the planet.

perfumes.name: Oud for Greatness
perfumes.description: Saffron-oud-musky power with Initio’s “functional” aura. Nuclear performance, unapologetic presence.

perfumes.name: Naxos
perfumes.description: Sicilian honey-tobacco bliss. Sweet, rich and impossibly smooth — the gourmand that launched a thousand clones.

perfumes.name: Alexandria II
perfumes.description: Fruity-oud opulence — apple and rose over precious woods. Regal and long-lived.

perfumes.name: Layton
perfumes.description: Apple-lavender-vanilla elegance. The refined sweet-fresh niche that never shouts.

perfumes.name: Pegasus
perfumes.description: Almond-powder sophistication. Heliotrope and bitter almond in a cloud of vanilla — distinctive and debonair.

perfumes.name: Hacivat
perfumes.description: The pineapple-fresh Aventus rival from Istanbul. Brighter, greener, and a performance monster in heat.

perfumes.name: Cool Water
perfumes.description: The original marine fresh. Calone-driven ocean breeze that defined 90s freshness and still sells in every Indian city.

perfumes.name: Light Blue
perfumes.description: Sicilian citrus-floral crispness. The definitive fresh women’s summer scent — endlessly cloned.

perfumes.name: The Most Wanted
perfumes.description: Toffee-ginger seduction. Sweet, warm and dangerously wearable — the modern gourmand-spicy hit.

perfumes.name: X for Men
perfumes.description: Old money in a bottle. Cardamom and orris over vetiver — quiet, crisp, impossibly refined British luxury.

perfumes.name: Ombre Nomade
perfumes.description: Raspberry-oud smoke drifting over desert incense. LV’s masterpiece of dark rosewood luxury.

perfumes.name: Cedrat Boise
perfumes.description: The citrus-oud benchmark. Sparkling lemon-blackcurrant over creamy sandalwood — a fruity-woody legend.

perfumes.name: Khamrah
perfumes.description: The viral gourmand. Spiced dates and praline in a boozy-sweet embrace — India’s favourite affordable luxury.

perfumes.name: Asad
perfumes.description: The Dior Sauvage Elixir rival from Dubai. Peppery tobacco-coffee darkness at a fraction of the price.

perfumes.name: Club de Nuit Intense Man
perfumes.description: The Aventus legend. Smoky birch-pineapple at drugstore money — the dupe that started a movement.

perfumes.name: Hawas for Him
perfumes.description: The fresh-aquatic king of Indian summers. Citrus-plum sparkle over salty musk — endlessly complimented.

perfumes.name: La Yuqawam
perfumes.description: Raspberry-oud leather opulence. Dark, rich, unapologetically Middle Eastern.

perfumes.name: 9PM
perfumes.description: The sweet night-out champion. Cinnamon-apple blossom melting into vanilla — unbeatable at the price.

perfumes.name: Amber Oud
perfumes.description: The BR540-adjacent amber. Melon-amber sweetness with serious presence — a dupe-culture staple.

dupeRelationships.verdict: Opens remarkably close to Baccarat Rouge 540, nailing the signature accord within minutes. The drydown is where the gap shows — EM5 BR 540 wears smoother and simpler, with less depth in the base. At roughly 1/2th the price, it is an easy recommendation for daily wear.

A faithful interpretation rather than a photocopy: EM5 Aqua captures the soul of Cool Water while wearing slightly sweeter and more modern. Performance is honest for the price — strong for 4–6 hours, then a skin scent.

reviews.title: The king, even in Delhi heat
reviews.body: Wore it to a wedding in May — 40 degrees and it still projected for 6 hours. Nothing else does that. Worth every rupee if you can stretch.

reviews.title: Great, but try the clones first
reviews.body: Beautiful smoky pineapple. That said, at this price please sample EM5 or Dupify versions before committing — you might be 85% happy for 2% of the price.

reviews.title: Office-safe beast
reviews.body: Two sprays for office, four for evenings. The ambroxan can get scratchy in peak summer afternoons — monsoon is its best season here.

reviews.title: Compliment magnet, no notes
reviews.body: Strangers ask about it. That almost never happens. Saffron-amber glow that lasts all day on clothes.

reviews.title: Viral for a reason
reviews.body: Spiced dates and praline — smells like a Goan Christmas. Lasts 10+ hours in Mumbai humidity. Best 1800 rupees in perfumery.

reviews.title: Chennai summer solved
reviews.body: The only fresh scent that survives our humidity past noon. Aquatic-plum-musk, endlessly wearable.

reviews.title: 85% there for 2% of the price
reviews.body: Side-by-sided with the original at a meetup. Opening is shockingly close; the drydown is simpler. For 499, absurd value.

reviews.title: Hawas on a budget
reviews.body: Fresh, clean, inoffensive — perfect gym/office scent. Lasts about 5 hours on skin, longer on clothes.

reviews.title: Polished and refined
reviews.body: You can tell the oil concentration is high — it wears dense and smooth. Office-perfect. Wish the bottle was bigger than 8ml.

reviews.title: Honey-tobacco heaven
reviews.body: The best thing I have smelled under 500 rupees. Rich, warm, addictive — winter essential.

reviews.title: Good, not great
reviews.body: Pleasant fruity-woody scent, but the smoky birch depth of the original is missing. Fine for the price, EM5 edges it in my testing.

reviews.title: Winter royalty
reviews.body: Too heavy for Indian summer, but December-January evenings? Unbeatable. Tobacco, vanilla, dried fruit — pure luxury.

reviews.title: Petrichor in a bottle
reviews.body: Smells exactly like the first rain on dry earth. Deeply Indian, deeply moving. A drop lasts all day.

reviews.title: Solid leather
reviews.body: Raspberry-leather done well. Not identical to the Tom Ford, but a genuinely good scent in its own right.

reviews.title: The legend delivers
reviews.body: Harsh first 20 minutes, then pure Aventus-adjacent glory. Let it macerate two weeks after buying — trust me.

reviews.title: Sauvage, but grown up
reviews.body: Denser, spicier, more refined than the EDT. The licorice note is divisive — sample first. Performance is elite.

articles.title: We lab-tested 5 Aventus dupes — here is the honest ranking
articles.excerpt: Five Indian alternatives to Creed Aventus, one blind panel, zero sponsorship. The winner surprised us.
articles.author: Scentiqa Lab
articles.body:
Creed Aventus costs roughly ₹24,500 in India. Every Indian clone house has an answer to it — but which answers are honest? Our five-person panel wore each dupe for a full day in 38°C Delhi heat, blind, and scored opening, drydown, longevity and sillage separately.

1. EM5’s interpretation (₹499) — our lab score: the highest of the batch. The smoky pineapple opening is strikingly close; only the drydown’s depth gives it away. Best value in the test by a mile.

2. Armaf Club de Nuit Intense Man (₹2,200) — the legend. Harsher opening than the rest, but the drydown is the closest thing to Aventus under ₹3,000. Let it macerate two weeks.

3. Dupify’s Aventus (₹599) — pleasant and fruity, but the birch smoke that defines Aventus is muted. A good scent; a less convincing clone.

4. Purenso’s Aventus oil (₹245) — remember this is an oil, not a spray. Intimate, long-lasting on skin, but it never projects like the original.

5. Celestial’s Aventus Noir (₹749) — community-suggested; our lab has not completed full testing yet. Early impressions are positive but unverified.

The takeaway: you can get 80%+ of the Aventus experience for under ₹1,000 in India today. That is exactly why Scentiqa exists.

articles.title: House of EM5: decoding the ₹499 phenomenon
articles.excerpt: How a Mumbai clone house became India’s gateway drug to niche perfumery.
articles.author: Scentiqa Editorial
articles.body:
Walk into any Indian fragrance community and ask where beginners should start. The answer, overwhelmingly, is three letters: EM5.

House of EM5’s playbook is disarmingly simple — take the world’s most-cloned scents (Baccarat Rouge 540, Cool Water, Hawas), bottle competent interpretations as 50ml EDPs, and sell them on Flipkart and Amazon for around ₹499. No mystique, no attar-shop theatrics.

Our lab testing puts their BR540 interpretation among the strongest value scores we have measured. The Hawas-inspired Ocean Breeze is arguably the best ₹499 fresh scent in the country for Indian summers.

Are they identical to the originals? No — and our claimed-vs-lab panels show exactly where the gaps are. But EM5 has done something the luxury houses never bothered to: make great-smelling perfumery accessible to a college student in Indore. That deserves respect.

articles.title: How to spot a fake Creed Aventus in India (2026 guide)
articles.excerpt: Grey-market Aventus floods Indian marketplaces. Here is how to protect yourself.
articles.author: Scentiqa Trust Team
articles.body:
Aventus is the most counterfeited niche perfume in India. If a deal looks too good — ₹8,000 for a 100ml “sealed” bottle — it is fake. Full stop.

Checklist:

1. Batch code: etched on the back of the bottle, matching the box. No sticker-only codes.
2. Atomizer: genuine Creed atomizers are precise and quiet; fakes sputter.
3. Juice color: Aventus varies by batch, but neon or murky juice is a red flag.
4. Seller: buy only from sellers on our verified list. Marketplace listings with stock photos and no GST invoice are the danger zone.

When in doubt, post photos in our Fakes Help Desk — the community authenticates dozens of bottles a week.

And remember: a great Indian dupe at ₹499 beats a fake “Aventus” at ₹8,000 every single time.

articles.title: Arabian Aroma’s original “Seduction” overtakes its dupes
articles.excerpt: The Kanpur house’s original creation is now its bestseller — a sign of India’s maturing clone market.
articles.author: Scentiqa Newsroom
articles.body:
Something interesting is happening in Kanpur. Arabian Aroma — the house that reportedly moved ~500,000 bottles in 2024 largely on inspired fragrances — says its original creation, Seduction, is now its bestselling scent.

It is a milestone worth noting. India’s clone houses began as pure alternatives to Western luxury; now the best of them are developing original identities. Seduction’s fruity-woody profile has earned a 4.5 community rating on Scentiqa, higher than most of the house’s inspired line.

The arc of every mature dupe market — from the Middle East to now India — bends from imitation to creation. We will be watching.

forum.name: Beginners’ Corner
forum.description: New to fragrance? Start here — no question is too basic.

topics.title: How many sprays is too many in Indian summer?
topics.author: desi_nose

posts.body: I do 4 sprays of Hawas and my colleagues say it’s strong. What’s the rule for 40-degree heat?
Heat amplifies projection. Rule of thumb: halve your winter sprays in May-June. 2-3 sprays max for fresh scents, 1-2 for heavy orientals.
Also: spray clothes, not just skin. It lasts longer and projects less aggressively in humidity.

topics.title: First niche purchase — Aventus or BR540?
topics.author: fraghead_mumbai

posts.body: Saved up 25k. Should I buy Aventus or BR540? I live in Mumbai.
Mumbai humidity + BR540 = you will smell amazing but you might suffocate others in locals. Aventus wears better in heat.
Honestly? Buy neither first. Spend 2k on EM5 BR540 + Armaf CDNIM + Hawas, live with the DNAs for a month, then decide.

forum.name: Dupe Talk
forum.description: Indian alternatives, clone houses, similarity debates.

topics.title: EM5 vs Dupify Aventus — final verdict?
topics.author: desi_nose

posts.body: Both claim to be the Aventus killer. Who wins?
Our lab scored EM5 higher on drydown match. Dupify’s opening is nice but fades faster. Full breakdown in the lab report article.
EM5 for me too. Also Dupify’s “95%” claim vs our lab’s number — always check the claimed-vs-lab panel.

topics.title: My Perfume Secrets accuracy claims — legit?
topics.author: priya_scent

posts.body: MPS prints “82% accuracy” on the Bleu listing. How is that measured?
It’s the house’s own claim — marketing, basically. Our lab independently scored it in the low 80s, so this one happens to be fair. Not all are.

forum.description: Traditional Indian perfumery — attars, ruhs, shamamas.

topics.title: Mitti attar recommendations for a beginner?
topics.author: scentofchennai

posts.body: I want to try the famous petrichor attar. Boond? Sugandhco?
Boond’s Maati is the crowd favourite and easy to find on Amazon. Apply one drop — attars are concentrated.
Second Boond. Also try their Ruh Gulab if you like florals.

topics.title: How do you wear attar without overdoing it?
topics.author: fraghead_mumbai

posts.body: One drop of shamama filled my whole office. Help.
Behind the ears and a touch on the wrists. Never more than two drops for potent ones like shamama or oudh.

topics.title: What did you wear today? (daily thread)
topics.author: arjun_sniffs

posts.body: Naxos. It’s October, finally cool enough.
MPS Naxos 2020 — the dupe, and honestly I’m not mad about it.
Hawas. Chennai doesn’t do October.
What survives Mumbai monsoon? My fresh scents die in 2 hours.
Ambroxan-heavy scents (Sauvage DNA) cut through humidity. Also: attars. Oils don’t wash out like alcohol sprays.

topics.title: Interlude Man in Indian summer — madness?
topics.author: arjun_sniffs

posts.body: One spray of Interlude in May cleared a room. Respect the beast.
It’s a November-to-February scent in India. Full stop.

topics.title: Is Xerjoff worth 3x Parfums de Marly?
topics.author: fraghead_mumbai

posts.body: Naxos vs Layton — both sweet, very different prices.
Different beasts. Naxos is honey-tobacco opulence; Layton is apple-lavender elegance. Try both via MPS/Naxos clones first for under 500.
